A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M-DESIGN research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are available and readable, supporting comparison across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-design experiments across graph tasks, tabular and image benchmarks, together with component ablations and refinement analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds repository-scale sensitivity, initialization sensitivity, and trajectory-AUC results.

M1.justification: The modification-gain graphs, knowledge weaving, Bayesian similarity updates, and predictive planners are retained. Added training, replay-buffer, and cold-start details document existing components without establishing an actual procedural change.

E1.justification: The matched graph, tabular, and image benchmark suites are unchanged. However, v3 Appendix B.3 newly reports offline model collection on Physics, which is absent from the dataset inventory. Whether this represents additional training coverage or a naming error is unresolved.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the matched experiments is unchanged. The new trajectory-AUC comparison uses the same seven baselines already included in the efficiency comparison in Table 2; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds trajectory AUC as an efficiency metric and controlled comparisons using 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of benchmark sources and three initialization strategies. Existing benchmark protocols retain the 100-evaluation budget and target-dataset exclusion.

E4.justification: New Table 4 tests sensitivity to MKB source retention, and Table 13 tests final accuracy under weighted-average, majority-vote, and most-similar initialization. Existing component ablations, OOD analyses, and initial-similarity cutoff experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten-trial averages, standard-deviation shading for stochastic refinement trajectories, and the same Shapiro–Wilk analysis. The added tables introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice or explicit increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Matched existing results are unchanged. New results include average accuracy of 81.50 with 25% MKB retention versus 82.11 with full retention, average trajectory AUC of 0.815 for M-DESIGN versus 0.811 for DesiGNN, and initialization averages of 81.80, 81.79, and 81.31. These are additional analyses, not improvements to existing same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Equation (5), corrects the stated optimization domain from the knowledge base K to the explicitly defined local candidate set Ct, aligning it with the local search already specified in v2. The gain-consistency assumptions and Appendix B.1 derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims about adaptive refinement, Bayesian transfer calibration, predictive planners, and reaching search-space optima in 26 of 33 cases. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new sensitivity results as graceful degradation with reduced repository coverage and stability across initialization choices. Its limitations now explicitly describe gain consistency as a local conditional-expectation assumption and predictive planners as an empirical fallback without a theorem-level guarantee.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information: it adds a method repository URL, planner pretraining settings, a size-10 FIFO replay buffer, and cold-start regression defaults maintained until three observations. New Appendix B.3 documents MKB and planner storage plus offline GPU costs. These are newly disclosed details, not established changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds Delta-NAS when discussing within-task performance-difference predictors and four works on GNN fine-tuning or knowledge-graph function search in Appendix A.3. Other numerous reference edits mainly update bibliographic metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: The core narrative is retained with local copyediting. v3 separates limitations and conclusion into Sections 6 and 7, adds appendix subsections and acknowledgements, and updates the corresponding-author and publication information.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4, 12, and 13 and relocates existing figures and tables as the document reflows. Existing figure artwork is retained; captions, spacing, and table numbering receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through implementation and resource disclosures, adds targeted robustness checks and an additional efficiency metric, and more clearly qualifies the predictive planners’ guarantees. These are useful, incremental gains while the core method and existing results remain stable. The new Physics construction-cost example remains unreconciled with the dataset inventory.
